about: The operator-owned meaning of the authorization boundary. The canonical inventory says what exists; this file says where each component belongs, what exists but is not inventoried, which services are leveraged from an existing authorization, and the data-flow table. scripts/build-boundary-graph.py applies it on every deploy to produce the signed /.well-known/boundary-map.json. Rules match inventory component_ids with shell-style globs (fnmatch); the first matching group wins. An inventory component no rule places is reported as unclassified, and the reconciliation gate fails the deploy on it: classify a new resource in the same change that adds it.

zones.label: Outside the boundary (Rules of Thumb #3 and #4)
Authorization boundary: Cloud Service Offering, internal components (sp-system)
In boundary: external services without FedRAMP authorization (Rule of Thumb #2)
Leveraged: services inherited from an existing FedRAMP authorization (sp-inherited)

groups.label: Code and models the app loads in the user's browser

declared.label: Operator (dev machine)
declared.why: Out per Rule of Thumb #4: development environment, no federal information.

declared.label: Operator email and SaaS
declared.why: Out per Rule of Thumb #3; receives the evidence-alarm email (flow I), which carries alarm metadata only.

declared.label: Public Internet (readers, verifiers)
declared.why: Anonymous consumers of the site and the /.well-known/ evidence.

declared.label: App users (Silk Reeling)
declared.why: Authenticated end users, via Cognito with mandatory TOTP MFA.

leveraged.name: AWS East/West
leveraged.why: Per Key Concept #6: the underlying infrastructure is inherited from the AWS package under the customer responsibility matrix.

flows.label: Operator → GitHub repository and Actions
flows.data: Source code, IaC configuration, content

flows.label: GitHub Actions → AWS APIs (deploy role)
flows.auth: GitHub OIDC → STS role; no static keys (privileged)
flows.data: Terraform plan and apply, AWS API calls

flows.label: Deploy → S3 (site and /.well-known/)
flows.encryption: In transit TLS; at rest SSE-S3
flows.data: Site content and /.well-known/ evidence

flows.label: Deploy → Lambda functions (code)
flows.data: Lambda deployment packages

flows.label: GitHub Actions → Sigstore Fulcio and Rekor
flows.data: CSR, ECDSA P-256 signature, transparency-log entry

flows.label: EventBridge → KSI emitter → S3 (daily)
flows.data: Runtime KSI signal (signed) write

flows.label: CloudFront → Public Internet
flows.data: Public site content and /.well-known/ evidence

flows.label: App user → API Gateway → app Lambda
flows.data: App requests: pose landmarks in, scores and feedback out (nothing leaves the boundary)

flows.label: Alarms → SNS topic → operator email (out)
flows.encryption: At rest: CMK · email not end-to-end encrypted
flows.data: Alarm metadata only (name, state, reason)

flows.label: Evidence Nightly → S3 (.well-known/vdr-*)
flows.auth: GitHub OIDC → STS; the role can write only .well-known/vdr-* (unattended)
flows.encryption: In transit TLS; at rest SSE-S3
flows.data: Refreshed VDR and trend, the nightly audit-log review and the monthly recovery exercises (Sigstore-signed); the audit-log review reads CloudTrail event history with cloudtrail:LookupEvents only

flows.label: Watchdog → S3 (evidence freshness read)
flows.auth: Watchdog Lambda role: s3:GetObject on the published evidence keys only
flows.data: Published evidence timestamps; results go out as CloudWatch metrics that drive flow I's alarms

flows.label: App user → Cognito Hosted UI (sign-in)
flows.auth: Password + required TOTP MFA; OAuth2 authorization code with PKCE
flows.encryption: In transit: TLS; user records at rest encrypted by Cognito
flows.data: Sign-in credentials and MFA code in; ID and access tokens out (email address in the user record)

flows.label: App user's browser → jsDelivr (MediaPipe runtime)
flows.data: Pinned MediaPipe JavaScript and WebAssembly in; the request carries the user's IP address and user agent only

flows.label: App user's browser → Google Cloud Storage (pose model)
flows.data: Pose-landmarker model file in; the request carries the user's IP address and user agent only

flows.label: Site bucket → access-log bucket (S3 server access logs)
flows.auth: Log bucket policy admits only the S3 logging service
flows.data: Request records for origin reads: requester IP, user agent, key, status

flows.label: CloudFront → access-log bucket (edge access records, 90 days)
flows.auth: Log delivery service, admitted by the log bucket policy for this account only
flows.encryption: In transit TLS; at rest SSE-S3
flows.data: Per request: date, time, edge location, country, method, path, status, bytes, cache result; no client IP, user agent, referrer, query string or cookie

flows.label: Deploy → access-log bucket (reads edge access records)
flows.auth: Deploy role (GitHub OIDC); read-only on the CloudFront log prefixes
flows.encryption: In transit TLS; at rest SSE-S3
flows.data: Edge access records in; only aggregate monthly counts of /.well-known/ and /trust/ requests are published

flows.label: CloudTrail → CloudTrail log bucket
flows.auth: Bucket policy admits only CloudTrail for this trail
flows.encryption: At rest: SSE-S3; log-file validation on
flows.data: Management events: API caller identity, source IP, action, parameters

flows.label: KSI emitter → its log group
flows.data: Emitter run logs (no customer data)
flows.note: Failed asynchronous invocations go to the dead-letter queue (flow R).

flows.label: KSI emitter → dead-letter queue (failed invocations)
flows.auth: Lambda execution role (sqs:SendMessage on the queue only)
flows.data: The failed scheduled event (no customer data); kept 14 days

flows.label: App Lambda → its log group
flows.data: Application logs: request metadata, errors

flows.label: API Gateway → access log group
flows.auth: Log resource policy admits API Gateway delivery
flows.data: API access records: request ID, source IP, time, method, route, status, response length

flows.label: Watchdog → its log group
flows.data: Watchdog run logs (artifact ages; no customer data)

flows.label: Operator → AWS console and APIs (with TOTP MFA)
flows.auth: Password + TOTP MFA (root and the operator IAM user; privileged)
flows.data: Administrative sign-in and AWS API calls (recorded by CloudTrail, flow P)

flows.label: Deploy and plan → Terraform state bucket
flows.encryption: In transit TLS; at rest SSE-S3
flows.data: Terraform state (configuration and resource attributes, including secret values)

flows.label: Deploy and plan → state lock table
flows.encryption: In transit TLS; at rest AWS-owned key
flows.data: Lock ID, holder and timestamp only

flows.label: Deploy and nightly → GitHub Advisory Database (Dependabot alerts)
flows.auth: Repository token that can read Dependabot alerts
flows.data: Open dependency alerts in (public advisory data)

flows.label: Deploy and nightly → CISA KEV catalog
flows.data: KEV catalog in (public)

flows.label: Deploy and nightly → FIRST EPSS scores
flows.data: EPSS scores file in (public)

flows.label: Deploy and nightly → Grype vulnerability database
flows.data: Vulnerability database in (public)

flows.label: Incident Reports → S3 (.well-known/incident-*)
flows.auth: GitHub OIDC → STS; the role can write only .well-known/incident-* (unattended)
flows.encryption: In transit TLS; at rest SSE-S3
flows.data: Incident log and IIR/OIR/FIR reports (Sigstore-signed)

flows.label: Package Maintenance → S3 (certification package objects)
flows.auth: GitHub OIDC → STS; the role can write only the named certification package objects and the quarterly issue prefixes (unattended)
flows.encryption: In transit TLS; at rest SSE-S3
flows.data: SDR, CPO, OCR, their readable views, the quarterly issue index, issued reports and snapshots (Sigstore-signed)
